\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There is an absolute integer $C\ge1$ such that every finite nonempty
simple graph $G$ satisfies
\[
 \ell(G)\le C h(G).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:bounded}
Suppose $|V(P)|\le n$, where $n\ge1$, and $f(P)\le r$, where $r\ge1$.
There is a distribution on stable sets $I$ such that
\[
 |I|\le\lceil n/r\rceil,
 \qquad \Pr(v\in I)=\frac1{2r}\quad(v\in V(P)).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded differences]\label{lem:concentration}
Let $Z$ be a function of $s\ge1$ independent finite random variables.
If changing one variable changes $Z$ by at most $b>0$, then
\[
 \Pr\bigl(|Z-\mathbb EZ|\ge u\bigr)
 \le2\exp\bigl(-u^2/(2sb^2)\bigr)\qquad(u>0).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cut test]\label{lem:cut-test}
Let $P$ be a $k$-connected graph on at most $n$ vertices, where $k$ is a
sufficiently large integer. Set
\[
 s=\left\lceil10(n/k)\log(2n)\right\rceil.
\]
There is a family of at most $(n+1)^{s+1}$ matchings, each of size
$\lfloor k/8\rfloor$, with the following property. If $U\subseteq V(P)$,
every vertex of $P$ has at least $k/2$ neighbors outside $U$, and fewer
than $k/32$ endpoints of each matching belong to $U$, then $P-U$ is
$\lfloor k/32\rfloor$-connected.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Eligible thinning]\label{small:eligible-thinning}
There is an absolute positive integer $B$ such that the following holds
for all sufficiently large integers $t$. Let $n,r$ be real parameters with
\[
 1\le n\le t^{11/10},\qquad \frac{t}{\log t}\le r\le4t,
\]
and let $P$ be a graph with $|V(P)|\le n$, $h(P)<t$, and $f(P)\le r$.
Set
\[
 N=\left\lceil Br\log\bigl(2\max\{1,t/r\}\bigr)\right\rceil.
\]
Suppose $E_1,\ldots,E_N\subseteq V(P)$ contain every vertex at least
$N/2$ times. There are stable sets $I_1,\ldots,I_N$ of $P$, each of size
at most $\lceil n/r\rceil$, such that
\[
 f\left(P-\bigcup_{j=1}^N(I_j\cap E_j)\right)\le r/2.
\]
The cutoff for $t$ is uniform over $P,n,r$ and the eligibility sets.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{small:concentration}
Take at most $q$ independent copies of the experiment
\eqref{small:remainder}. Let $Z$ be any one of the following quantities,
where the vertex set $A\subseteq V(P)$ is fixed before sampling:
\[
 |A\cap W_i|,\qquad
 \left|A\cap\bigcup_iW_i\right|,\qquad
 f(P[A\cap W_i]).
\]
For each fixed $\delta>0$, and all sufficiently large $t$,
\begin{equation}\label{small:uniform-tail}
 \Pr\bigl(|Z-\mathbb EZ|\ge\delta r\bigr)
 \le2\exp(-t^{7/10}),
\end{equation}
uniformly over all the data in \eqref{small:range} and all eligibility
sets satisfying the stated condition.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{list:elementary}
The following hold for every finite graph $P$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $H$ is a subgraph of $P$, then $\ell(H)\le \ell(P)$.
\item For every $Z\subseteq V(P)$,
\[
\ell(P-Z)\ge \ell(P)-|Z|.
\]
\item If $P$ is $q$-degenerate, where $q$ is a nonnegative integer, then
$\ell(P)\le q+1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[List connectivity extraction]\label{lem:list-extraction}
For every integer $k\ge1$, if $\ell(P)>6k$, then some induced
$k$-connected subgraph $H$ of $P$ satisfies
\[
\ell(H)\ge\ell(P)-6k.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{list:high-neighbor-count}
Let $t\ge2$ be an integer, let $h(P)<t$, and let $X\subseteq V(P)$. Then
\[
\bigl|\{v\in V(P)\setminus X:|N_P(v)\cap X|\ge t\}\bigr|
\le\binom{|X|}{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Additive list-coloring loss]\label{lem:additive-deletion}
Let $L\ge1$ be the integer constant in Proposition~\ref{prop:small-list}.
For each fixed integer $d\ge0$, put
\[
c_d=4L+d+5.
\]
For every sufficiently large integer $t$, the following holds. Suppose
$h(P)<t$ and $X,Y\subseteq V(P)$ are disjoint sets such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $|X|\le t^{11/10}$;
\item $P[Y]$ is $dt$-degenerate;
\item every vertex outside $X\cup Y$ has at most $dt$ neighbors in $Y$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
\ell(P-X-Y)\ge\ell(P)-c_dt.
\]
The cutoff is independent of $P$, its order, and all list assignments and
their palettes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:coarse-density}
There is an absolute constant \(C_*>0\), for example \(C_*=10^4\),
such that, for every integer \(t\ge2\)
and every nonempty graph \(P\) with \(h(P)<t\),
\[
 d(P)\le C_*t\log(2t).
\]
Consequently, every graph \(P\) with \(h(P)<t\) satisfies
\[
 \ell(P)\le 2C_*t\log(2t)+1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:district}
For every fixed positive integer \(K\), there is an integer
\[
 D_K>\max(400B_*,12800K)
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large integers \(t\), every nonempty
graph \(P\) with
\[
 h(P)<t,\qquad d(P)\ge D_Kt
\]
contains an induced \((Kt)\)-connected subgraph of order at most
\(t^{1.06}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}\label{density:list-district}
Fix \(K\) and \(D_K\) as in Lemma~\ref{lem:district}.
For all sufficiently large integers \(t\), if
\[
 h(P)<t,\qquad \ell(P)>2D_Kt+2,
\]
then \(P\) contains an induced \((Kt)\)-connected subgraph of order
at most \(t^{1.06}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Vertex path packing]\label{lem:packing}
Let $A,B$ be disjoint vertex sets in a graph $P$, and let $j\ge1$ be an
integer.  Suppose that for every $X\subseteq V(P)$ with $|X|<j$, the graph
$P-X$ contains a path from $A\setminus X$ to $B\setminus X$.
Then there are $j$ pairwise vertex-disjoint paths from distinct vertices of
$A$ to distinct vertices of $B$.  Each path can be chosen to meet $A\cup B$
only at its two ends.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Two paths from every source]\label{lem:double-packing}
Let $A,B$ be disjoint vertex sets in a graph $P$, where $r=|A|\ge1$.
If $P$ is $2r$-connected and $|B|\ge2r$, there are two paths starting at
each vertex of $A$, ending at $2r$ distinct vertices of $B$, with no
intersections other than the two paths sharing their prescribed start.
Their internal vertices lie outside $A\cup B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rerouting through a woven district]\label{lem:rerouting}
Let $J$ be an $(a,b)$-woven subgraph of a graph $P$, and prescribe $a$
distinct roots in $J$.  Let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_q$ be vertex-disjoint paths in $P$,
where $q\le b$.  Orient each path arbitrarily.  For every path meeting
$J$, let $x_i,y_i$ be its first and last vertices in $J$.
There are vertex-disjoint paths $Q'_1,\ldots,Q'_q$ with the same
respective endpoints, and a model rooted at the prescribed roots in $J$,
such that the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item every vertex added to a path belongs to $J$; more precisely,
      $V(Q'_i)\setminus V(J)\subseteq V(Q_i)\setminus V(J)$;
\item a path originally disjoint from $J$ is unchanged;
\item the intersection of $Q'_i$ with the model is contained in the
      prescribed roots among $x_i,y_i$.
\end{enumerate}
The construction can be applied successively in disjoint districts.
If some prescribed roots are endpoints of the original path system,
the bags for these roots meet the resulting paths only at their own
roots, including after all subsequent replacements in other districts.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Small districts are woven]\label{lem:small-woven}
For all sufficiently large integers $t$, every $(K_0t)$-connected graph
$J$ of order at most $t^{1.06}$ is $(s,3t)$-woven whenever
\[
 1\le s\le 2\left\lceil\frac{t}{(\log t)^2}\right\rceil.
\]
The cutoff is absolute and uniform in $s$ and $J$.  No minor-exclusion
hypothesis on $J$ is required.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Combining paths by pairing temporary sources]
\label{lem:combine}
Let $Z,D,V(H)$ be pairwise disjoint vertex sets in a graph $P$, and let
$m\ge1$.  Suppose there are:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item two paths from each vertex of $Z$ to distinct vertices of $D$,
      with all target ends distinct, with intersections only at their
      prescribed repeated starts, and avoiding $V(H)$;
\item $2m$ vertex-disjoint paths from distinct vertices of $H$ to
      distinct vertices of $D$, avoiding $Z$ and meeting $H$ only at
      their starting vertices.
\end{enumerate}
Then, using only vertices of these two families, one can obtain
$|Z|+m$ vertex-disjoint paths to distinct vertices of $D$, one starting
at each vertex of $Z$ and one starting at each of $m$ distinct vertices
of $H$.  These paths meet $D$ and $H$ only at their appropriate ends.
Moreover, after any partition of the $2m$ second-family starts into $m$
pairs, the $m$ selected starts in $H$ can be required to include exactly
one vertex from each pair.  No unselected second-family start is visited
by any of the resulting paths.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Separability]
\label{lem:separability}
There is an absolute positive integer \(S\) such that, for all sufficiently
large integers \(t\), every graph \(G\) satisfying
\[
 h(G)<t,\qquad r=\ell(G)\ge 2St
\]
has two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs \(G_1,G_2\) with
\[
 \ell(G_1),\ell(G_2)\ge r-St.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Deleting a history of paths]
\label{separate:footprint}
Let \(h(G)<t\). Start with \(F_0=W_0\), where \(|W_0|=t\), and perform
at most \(R_t\) rounds with the following rules. At the start of a round
there is a footprint \(F\) and a set \(W\subseteq F\) of \(t\) tips.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Choose disjoint sets \(J,D\subseteq V(G)\setminus F\), each of
size at most \(t^{1.06}\), and a set \(R\subseteq J\) of at most \(t\)
vertices. Put \(Z=W\cup R\).
\item In the induced graph \(G-(F\setminus W)\), choose a
minimum-total-length double system \(\mathcal Q_1\) from \(Z\) to \(D\):
two paths from each vertex of \(Z\), otherwise vertex-disjoint, with
distinct target ends. Set
\[
 F^- =F\cup J\cup D\cup V(\mathcal Q_1).
\]
\item Choose a source set \(A\subseteq V(G)\setminus F^-\). In the
induced graph \(G-(F\cup R)\), choose a minimum-total-length system
\(\mathcal Q_2\) of \(2t\) vertex-disjoint paths from arbitrary distinct
vertices of \(A\) to arbitrary distinct vertices of \(D\). Set
\[
 F^+=F^-\cup V(\mathcal Q_2),
\]
and choose \(t\) tips \(W^+\subseteq F^+\) for the next round.
\end{enumerate}
Only histories in which the indicated systems exist are considered.
The final round may end after step \textup{(ii)}.

There is an absolute integer
\begin{equation}
 \label{separate:cf}
 c_f=c_{6B_*+20}=4L+6B_*+25
\end{equation}
such that, for all sufficiently large \(t\), every final footprint
\(F_{\rm last}\) of such a history satisfies
\[
 \ell(G-F_{\rm last})\ge\ell(G)-c_ft.
\]
The same assertion holds for the initial footprint.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[A bounded weight evaluator]\label{prop:weight-evaluator}
Given a profile in the entire slice $\mathcal S$, rational
$0<\rho,\beta<1$, and a rational power $s\in[0,1]$ with denominator
$q_s$, there is an evaluator using fresh random bits and returning a strictly positive rational
$\widehat h_s$ such that
\[
 \PP\bigl[(1-\rho)h^s\le\widehat h_s\le(1+\rho)h^s\bigr]
       \ge1-\beta.
\]
Its output length, number of rank queries, and other bit operations
are bounded on every execution by fixed polynomials in $N$, the
input encoding lengths, $\rho^{-1}$, $\log(\beta^{-1})$, and $q_s$.
In particular an equally spaced schedule with a polynomial number of
phases has polynomially bounded denominators. Moreover $J$ admits
a deterministic positive rational approximation $\widehat J$ with
$|\log(\widehat J/J)|\le N^{-7}$ in polynomial work.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Prefixes and part totals]\label{lem:generator-prefixes}
Let \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_m)\) be a family of subsets of \(E\).
Its atoms admit an order such that every prefix is a union of at most
\(n\) intersections of members of \(\mathcal A\), allowing \(E\) as
the empty intersection.  If \(s\) is normalized, nonnegative, and submodular,
\(s(E)=0\), and \(s(A_j)\le b\) for every \(j\), where \(b\ge0\),
then in this order
every prefix \(F\) satisfies
\[
 s(F)\le n(m+1)b.
\]
Consequently, suppose that \(Q\subseteq B(r)\) and
\(r(A_j)-x(A_j)\le b\) for all \(x\in Q\) and all \(j\).
For every atom \(D\) of \(\mathcal A\) and every \(x,y\in Q\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part-range}
 |x(D)-y(D)|\le 2n(m+1)b.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Refinement witnesses]\label{lem:refinement-witnesses}
Fix integer \(w\) for which both \(Q_i(w)\) are nonempty.
For each system separately, its lattice points and those of its
expanded slice can be partitioned by fixing integer totals on
successively finer parts.  Each resulting original slice has the
form
\[
 Q=\{x\in B(r_i):x(D)=v_D\ (D\in\mathcal P)\},
\]
where \(\mathcal P\) refines \(\mathcal G\) and every part of
\(\mathcal P\) is a union of \(\mathcal D_i\)-parts.  Its
expanded partner is exactly \(Q+\Delta_i\).  Every nonempty
terminal slice has a point \(a^*\in Q\) satisfying
\begin{align}
 \|a^*-c\|_\infty&\le N^{60}S,
                       \label{eq:witness-distance}\\
 r_i(A)-a^*(A)&\ge S
       &&\text{if \(A\) cuts a part of \(\mathcal P\)},
                       \label{eq:witness-terminal-slack}\\
 r_i(A)-a^*(A)&\ge W/2
       &&\text{if \(A\) cuts a part of \(\mathcal D_i\)}.
                       \label{eq:witness-fine-slack}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There is a single uniform randomized algorithm which, for every input
described above, outputs a nonnegative rational $\widehat Z$ satisfying
\[
 \PP\bigl((1-\eps)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\eps)Z\bigr)
 \ge1-\delta.
\]
If $Z=0$, the algorithm outputs zero on every execution. On every
execution, both its number of oracle calls and its number of other bit
operations are bounded by one fixed polynomial in
\[
 n,\qquad \ell,\qquad \eps^{-1},\qquad \log(\delta^{-1}).
\]
The bit-operation bound includes rational arithmetic, generation of
independent unbiased random bits, and the encoding of the output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Oracle algorithms]\label{prop:oracle-tools}
The following operations have deterministic oracle and bit complexity
bounded by fixed polynomials in the indicated input sizes.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item An integer-valued submodular function on a finite ground set can
 be minimized, with a minimizing set returned, from an exact value oracle
 and a bound on the binary lengths of its values.  The size parameters are
 the ground-set cardinality and that value-length bound.
 \item Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded rational polytope, supplied
 by strong separation, a coordinate bound, and a bound on the binary
 encoding length of each individual defining inequality.  The separator
 returns inequalities of length polynomial in the query length and
 the supplied description bounds.  Exact rational
 linear optimization, including an emptiness decision and the production
 of an optimal vertex when $Q$ is nonempty, is polynomial in $d$, these
 bounds, and the objective length.  This assertion includes
 lower-dimensional polytopes.  All separation queries have polynomial
 encoding length.
\end{enumerate}
The first operation also applies to an integer submodular function with
a rational modular term added, and with prescribed elements required to
belong or not to belong to the minimizing set.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Base-polytope identities]\label{lem:base-calculus}
Let $f,g:2^E\to\mathbb R$ be normalized submodular functions and let
$v\in\mathbb R^E$.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item If $w_{\pi(1)}\geq\cdots\geq w_{\pi(n)}$ and
 $A_k=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k)\}$, the vector
 \[
 b_{\pi(k)}=f(A_k)-f(A_{k-1})
 \]
 belongs to $B(f)$ and maximizes $w\cdot x$ there.
 \item With $(f+v)(A)=f(A)+v(A)$ and
 $f^{\mathrm{ref}}(A)=f(E\setminus A)-f(E)$, one has
 \[
 B(f+g)=B(f)+B(g),\qquad B(f+v)=B(f)+v,\qquad
 B(f^{\mathrm{ref}})=-B(f).
 \]
 \item For a partition $\mathcal D$ of $E$, define
 $\pi_{\mathcal D}(x)=(x(D):D\in\mathcal D)$ and
 $\bar f(\mathcal J)=f(\bigcup_{D\in\mathcal J}D)$.
 Then $\pi_{\mathcal D}(B(f))=B(\bar f)$.
 \item For distinct $a,b\in E$ and $t\geq0$, the segment
 $[-t,t](e_a-e_b)$ is $B(q_{ab})$, where
 \[
 q_{ab}(A)=t\,|\mathbf1_A(a)-\mathbf1_A(b)|.
 \]
 In particular, adding any collection of these segments to a base
 polytope again gives a base polytope, with integral rank if $f$ and
 the segment lengths are integral.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polyhedral controls]\label{lem:polyhedral-controls}
Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^E$ be nonempty and be defined either by
$B(f_1)\cap B(f_2)$ or by $B(f)$ together with equations
$x(D)=a_D$ for the parts $D$ of a partition of $E$.
The functions are normalized and submodular.  In either case arbitrary
coordinate lower and upper bounds may also be imposed.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item If the ranks and all other right sides are integral, every
 vertex of $Q$ is integral.
 \item Suppose $x\in\mathbb R^E$ satisfies every defining inequality
 with additive violation at most $b\geq0$, and every defining equality
 with absolute error at most $b$.  Then
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:polyhedral-distance}
  \operatorname{dist}_{\infty}(x,Q)\leq10(n+1)^2b.
 \end{equation}
 \item Fix $a\in Q$ and an affine function $F$ whose linear part is
 integral.  The function
 \[
  \phi(l)=\max\{F(y):y\in Q,\ \|y-a\|_\infty\leq l\},
  \qquad l\geq0,
 \]
 is continuous, nondecreasing, concave, and piecewise affine.  Every
 positive slope of an affine piece is an integer and hence at least
 one.  Eventually $\phi(l)=\max_Q F$.
 Consequently, if $F\geq0$ on $Q$ and $\phi(L)<L$ for some $L>0$,
 then $\phi(L)=\max_QF$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integral tree coordinates]\label{lem:tree-coordinates}
There is a unique pair $X_i(u,z)$ with these properties and
$X_{1e}=z_e$ on nontree edges. Its coordinates are integral linear
functions of $(u,z)$, with coefficients of absolute value at most
$10(n+1)$. Each coordinate depends only on variables in its superblock.
For integral $(u,z)$ this is a bijection onto integral pairs with the
specified $\mathcal D_1$-totals for $X_1$ and $\mathcal D_2$-totals
for $X_2$, and with $X_1-X_2$ supported on the representatives.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[What the penalties enforce]\label{lem:port-penalties}
An original base pair with a representative shift satisfies
\eqref{eq:hard-port-conditions} and $\sum_GV_G\le N^7S$.
Conversely, if~\eqref{eq:hard-port-conditions} holds, then
\[
 X_i(A)-r_i(A)\le\sum_G V_G\qquad(A\subseteq E, i=1,2).
\]
If in addition $\sum_GV_G\le T$, then $X_i\in B_i^+$ for both $i$,
where $B_i^+$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:expanded-bases}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[The positive port model]\label{prop:port-model}
For every nonempty input after the deterministic feasibility test,
the preceding construction gives at most $2n$ paired ports of lengths
$d_{iD}\le N^{21}W$, with $p=\sum d_{iD}$ polynomial in $N$, and a
strictly positive weight $h$ on the entire slice~\eqref{eq:paired-count-slice}.
For every real $s\in[0,1]$, $h^s$ has both integer signatures of
Definition~\ref{def:integer-signatures}. Its balanced mass
\[
 \mathcal Z_{\rm port}
   =\sum_{\substack{(a,b)\in\mathcal S\\
                    a_{iD}+b_{iD}=d_{iD}\ \forall(i,D)}}h(a,b)
\]
satisfies
$|\log(\mathcal Z_{\rm port}/(JZ))|\le100N^{-7}$.
These statements include $p=0$, when there is a single profile.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Balanced summation]
\label{lem:balanced-summation}
Let $F>0$ on the entire slice $\mathcal B(m,r)$ and suppose it has
the removal signature.  Choose disjoint coordinate pairs
$\{a_t,b_t\}$ with $m_{a_t}=m_{b_t}=M_t\ge1$.
Their balanced sum
\[
 \Phi(z)=\sum_{0\le k_t\le M_t}
 F\bigl(z,(k_t,M_t-k_t)_t\bigr)
\]
is strictly positive on the entire remaining box slice of total
$r-\sum_tM_t$ and has the removal signature.
The same statement holds with ``addition'' in place of ``removal''.
Fixing coordinates at prescribed box-valid values preserves either
signature and positivity on the resulting valid slice.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rank-factor signatures]
\label{lem:rank-signatures}
Partition a set of count coordinates $I$ into groups indexed by $E$,
allowing empty groups, and let $b\in\Z_{\ge0}^E$.
For either of the two consistent orientations
\[
 v_e=b_e+\sum_{i\text{ in group }e}z_i,
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 v_e=b_e+\sum_{i\text{ in group }e}(m_i-z_i),
\]
the factor $G(z)=\Phi_{r,H}(v)$ satisfies
$\one\one^{\mathsf T}-Q\succeq0$ for both signs in
\eqref{eq:signature-normalization}.
The product of such factors on disjoint sets of count coordinates
has both integer signatures on every total slice.  The assertion
holds for every nonnegative power of the product, and for any
coordinates fixed at box-valid values.

More generally, a base constraint for an arbitrary integral
normalized submodular rank, with a fixed integer translation and
either consistent orientation of its grouped arguments on a finite
box, can be imposed as a limit of factors of this kind.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Root-direction log-concavity]
\label{prop:shift-logconcavity}
Let $f_1,f_2$ be integral normalized submodular functions on $E$,
not necessarily nondecreasing, and define
\[
 Y(d)=\#\{(x_1,x_2)\in(B(f_1)\cap\Z^E)\times
                         (B(f_2)\cap\Z^E):x_1-x_2=d\}.
\]
For $d_0\in\Z^E$ and distinct $j,k\in E$, put
$y(t)=Y(d_0+t(e_j-e_k))$, $t\in\Z$.
The positive support of $y$ is an integer interval, possibly
empty or a singleton.  For integers $a<t<b$ with
$y(a),y(b)>0$,
\begin{equation}
 y(t)\ge y(a)^{(b-t)/(b-a)}y(b)^{(t-a)/(b-a)}.
 \label{eq:shift-interpolation}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Local weight adjustment]
\label{lem:adjustment}
For every integer $r\ge4$ there are constants $A=A(r)>0$,
$B=B(r)\ge1$, and $\Lambda_r\ge1$ with the following property.
Let $\Lambda\ge\Lambda_r$, and let $H$ be a finite $K_r$-free graph
whose vertex set has a partition $\mathcal D$ such that each vertex has
at most one neighbor in each part.  For any positive vertex weights
with $s_i\le\Lambda$, there is a finite family of the multiplier and
drop operations defined above, with vectors $g^{(j)}$, listed supports
$J_j$, and rates $a_j\ge0$, such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:adjustment}
 t_i+\sum_j a_jg_i^{(j)}\le B d_i,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j:\,i\in J_j}a_j\le\Lambda^4
 \qquad(i\in V(H)).
\end{equation}
The constants depend only on $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Local cross estimate]
\label{lem:local-cross}
Assume the prices satisfy \eqref{eq:dual-test}, and fix a level $b$.
Let $S,D\subseteq V(H_b)$, where $S\cup D$ is contained in a ball of
radius $R_0$ in $H$ and meets every part of $\mathcal D$ in at most
$P_0$ vertices.  Suppose that
\[
 32\le h\le20\ell_0^2,\qquad q(S),q(D)\le e^h,
 \qquad 0\le\eta\le2,
\]
and that $\alpha_i,\beta_i\le\eta$ for $i\in S$.  If $A$ in
\eqref{eq:adjustment-parameters} is sufficiently large depending only
on $r$, then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:local-cross}
 e_{q,H_b}(S,D)\le C_1\bigl(\eta hq(S)+e^{-3h}\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $C_1=C_1(r)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Transfer under vertex splitting]
\label{lem:local-cross-transfer}
Let $F$ be a graph with a homomorphism $p:F\to H_b$ that is injective
on directed edges.  Give every vertex of $F$ the weight, prices,
coefficients, and part of its image.  Then every vertex of $F$ has at
most one neighbor in each inherited part.  Moreover,
\eqref{eq:local-cross} holds in $F$ for any $S,D\subseteq V(F)$
satisfying the mass and coefficient hypotheses of
Lemma~\ref{lem:local-cross}, provided $S\cup D$ lies in a ball of
radius $R_0$ in $F$ and meets each inherited part in at most $P_0$
vertices.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[Triangle bound]
\label{prop:triangle-bound}
For the graphs $H_b$, weights $q$, and prices constructed above from
\eqref{eq:dual-test}, with $A$ chosen as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:local-cross}, the quantities in
\eqref{eq:price-mass} and \eqref{eq:dyadic-triangle-mass} satisfy
\[
 T_0\le O_r(M_x).
\]
The implicit constant depends only on $r$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
For every integer $r\ge4$ there are constants $C_r>0$ and $\Delta_r\ge3$
such that every $K_r$-free graph $G$ of maximum degree
$\Delta\ge\Delta_r$ satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{DP}}(G)
 \le \left\lceil C_r\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\right\rceil.
\]
The constants depend only on $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:forbidden}
For every finite graph $F$ there are constants $C_F>0$ and
$\Delta_F\ge3$ such that every $F$-free graph $G$ of maximum degree
$\Delta\ge\Delta_F$ satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{DP}}(G)
 \le \left\lceil C_F\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\right\rceil.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Splitting a level graph]
\label{lem:triangle-splitting}
Let $32\le\ell\le\ell_0$, and let $F$ be a nonempty finite graph with no isolated
vertices, with a homomorphism into some $H_b$ injective on directed edges.
Give its vertices the inherited weights, prices, and parts, and suppose
that \eqref{eq:prepared-level} holds.  There is a graph $F'$ obtained by
splitting vertices and retaining at most one copy of each edge of $F$,
with unchanged vertex weights, such that every neighborhood of $F'$ has
weight at most $e^{\sqrt\ell}$ and
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\{a,u,v\}\text{ a triangle of }F'}q_aq_uq_v
 \ge \left(1-C_2\frac{\log\ell}{\sqrt\ell}\right)
       \sum_{\{a,u,v\}\text{ a triangle of }F}q_aq_uq_v,
 \label{eq:split-retention}
\end{equation}
where $C_2$ depends only on $r$.  The projection $F'\to F$ is a
homomorphism injective on directed edges.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Laminar spanning family]
\label{geom:lem-laminar}
Suppose \(x\in P(G)\) and \(x_e>0\) for every edge. There is a
laminar family \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal S_x\) whose cut
vectors are linearly independent and span all the cut vectors
\(\chi_S\), \(S\in\mathcal S_x\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Separable entropy bounds by covariance]
\label{a:thm-separable}
Let \(G\) be a finite loopless labelled multigraph of even order
\(n=2m\), with a nonempty perfect-matching family. With natural
logarithms and continuous endpoint conventions, define
\[
 J_c(x)=F(x)-cB(x)
   =\sum_{e\in E}\bigl[-x_e\ln x_e+c(1-x_e)\ln(1-x_e)\bigr].
\]
For each \(c\in\{3,4\}\) and every \(x\in P(G)\),
\begin{equation}\label{a:eq-separable-bounds}
 J_c(x)\le H(x)\le F(x)+B(x).
\end{equation}
For \(n=0\), all displayed quantities are zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[An exact partition of the ambient edges]\label{cons:legacy-partition}
If the entire edge set of a loopless labelled graph on $2m>0$ vertices
is partitioned by $k\ge1$ perfect matchings, then
\[
 N(G)\ge\bigl[k\exp\{-8(1-1/k)\}\bigr]^m\ge(e^{-8}k)^m.
\]
When $k=1$ the count is exactly one. If $k=0$ and the order is positive,
the graph is edgeless and its count is zero; only the coarse bound is
then asserted. On the empty vertex set there is one empty matching.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}
\label{c:prop-loops}
There is one deterministic algorithm which, given a graph on \(n\)
vertices with nonnegative binary integer pair and singleton-loop
multiplicities, returns a nonnegative rational number
\(A_{\mathrm{loop}}\) such that
\[
             \frac{N_{\mathrm{loop}}}{2^{18n}}
                  \le A_{\mathrm{loop}}\le N_{\mathrm{loop}}.
\]
It returns zero exactly when \(N_{\mathrm{loop}}=0\).
Its running time and output length are polynomial in the input bit
length, including when the input gives \(n\) in binary and lists only
the positive pair and loop records.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic approximate counting]
\label{thm:main}\label{thm:algorithm-guarantee}
There is one uniform deterministic algorithm which, on a graph on $n$
vertices with nonnegative binary integer pair multiplicities, returns an
integer $A\ge0$ satisfying
\[
                         N(G)/512^n\le A\le N(G).
\]
Its running time and output length are polynomial in the input bit length.
In particular, $A=0$ exactly when $N(G)=0$. The guarantee includes a compact
input consisting of binary $n$ and a list of positive pair records.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional components]\label{ent:components}
For $x\in P(G)$, remove its zero edges and the endpoints of its value-one
edges. Let the nonempty connected components of the remaining graph have
$2m_i$ vertices, and let $B_i$ denote the sum defining $B$ on component $i$.
Then
\[
                 F(x)-\sum_i(2-2/m_i)B_i(x)\le H(x)\le F(x).
\]
If there are no remaining components, $F(x)=B(x)=H(x)=0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Regular graphs with large odd cuts]
\label{cons:regular}
Let \(G\) be a finite loopless \(k\)-regular multigraph on \(2m>0\)
vertices, where \(k\ge1\). Suppose
\(\lvert\delta(S)\rvert\ge k\) for every odd vertex set \(S\).
Then the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{cons:structural} hold.
In particular, they hold for every \((k-1)\)-edge-connected
\(k\)-regular graph of positive even order.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Feasibility repair]
\label{d:lem-feasibility-repair}
Set \(A_0=10n^2\).  For every \(x\in[0,1]^p\), there is \(y\in P\) such that
\[
\|y-x\|_\infty\le (2+A_0)w(x).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact penalty and integral supergradients]
\label{d:lem-exact-penalty}
The function \(\Phi\) is concave on \([0,1]^p\), and
\[
\max_{x\in[0,1]^p}\Phi(x)=f^*.
\]
At every point of the box, \(\Phi\) has an integral supergradient \(g\)
satisfying \(\|g\|_2^2\le D_0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[An integral two-terminal minimum cut]
\label{d:lem-unit-mincut}
For distinct \(a,b\in W\), a minimum cut separating \(a\) from \(b\)
can be found deterministically using at most \(C\) unit augmentations
and \(O(v^2(C+1))\) arithmetic operations on integers of
\(O(\log_2(v+C+2))\) bits.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Minimum odd-terminal cut]
\label{d:lem-odd-cut-oracle}
Let \(U\subseteq W\) have positive even cardinality.  One can
deterministically find a set \(S\subseteq W\) minimizing \(c(S)\)
subject to \(|S\cap U|\) being odd.  The algorithm returns the set itself,
uses at most \(|U|-1\) recursive instances, and requires
\(O(|U|^3v^2(C+1))\) arithmetic operations on integers of
\(O(\log_2(v+C+2))\) bits.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The face of a triangle expansion]
\label{ex:lem-expansion-face}
The set
\[
 Q_T=\{y\in P(G'):y(\delta(T))=1\}
\]
is a face of \(P(G')\) affinely isomorphic to \(P(G)\). Under this
isomorphism an old edge keeps its coordinate and
\[
 y_{f_i}=y_{e_i}\qquad(1\le i\le3).
\]
If \(x\in P(G)\) has coordinate \(1/3\) on every edge, its image
\(x'\) has coordinate \(1/3\) on every edge of \(G'\).
The isomorphism maps the minimal face at \(x\) onto the minimal
face at \(x'\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Restriction on a universal entropy coefficient]
\label{ex:cor-coefficient}
If a constant \(c\) satisfies
\[
 H(x)\ge F(x)-cB(x)
\]
for every finite loopless multigraph \(G\) and every
\(x\in P(G)\), then
\[
 c\ge\frac{\ln3}{2\ln(3/2)}.
\]
The same necessary bound holds if the assertion is restricted to
simple graphs.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Unshifted rank and exact lifts]
\label{cor:exact-lift}
There are constants $c_0>0$ and $n_1$ such that, for every even
$n\ge n_1$, both $A_n(0)$ and $T_n(0)$ have real PSD rank at least
$2^{c_0n}$, and every exact semidefinite lift of $P_n$ has size at
least $2^{c_0n}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}\label{smooth:lem-dimension}
For each fixed integer \(d\ge1\) and all sufficiently large \(N\),
every irreducible constituent of the complexification of
\(\mathcal P_d^\perp\) has dimension at least
\[
 c_dN^{d/2},\qquad c_d=\frac1{2^dd!}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Three-cell smoothing]\label{cor:three-cell}
For every fixed $K>0$, there are an integer $d\ge1$ and $N_0$ with the following property. Let $N\ge N_0$ be even, and let $a,b,c$ be positive integers summing to $N$. For a uniform ordered partition into cells of these sizes, prescribe $x,y,z$ edges between the first and second, first and third, and second and third cells, respectively. Assume that $x,y,z$ are nonnegative integers and that
\[
 a-x-y,\qquad b-x-z,\qquad c-y-z
\]
are nonnegative even integers. Let $T_{x,y,z}$ average functions on perfect matchings subject to these counts, and let $\Pi_d$ project onto the edge-product span of degree at most $d$, using uniform measures as above. Then
\[
 \normop{T_{x,y,z}(I-\Pi_d)}\le N^{-K}
\]
uniformly in all the sizes and admissible triples. For every fixed partition and matching function $f$, the values $T_{x,y,z}\Pi_df$ are given by one polynomial of total degree at most $d$ in $(x,y,z)$ across all admissible triples.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Normalization of PSD factors]
\label{lem:normalization}
Let $S$ be a finite nonzero nonnegative matrix with entries at most $B$.
If $S$ admits a real PSD factorization of size $r_0$, it admits one
of size $r\le r_0$ whose row factors $F_a$ and column factors $G_m$
satisfy
\[
 \tr F_a\le B,\qquad \tr G_m\le r.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[A functional separating low-degree squares]
  \label{prop:parity-functional}
  For every sufficiently large even \(t\), let \(H\), \(Y\), and
  \(f_\epsilon\) be as above, and put \(D=\lfloor\tau t\rfloor\).
  There is a real linear functional \(\mathcal D\) on the space of all
  real functions on \(Y\) such that
  \begin{align}
    \mathcal D(1)&=1,
      \label{eq:parity-functional-one}\\
    \mathcal D(g^2)&\geq0
      &&\text{if \(g\) has block degree at most \(D\)},
      \label{eq:parity-functional-positivity}\\
    \mathcal D(f_\epsilon)&=-\epsilon
      &&(\epsilon>0),
      \label{eq:parity-functional-value}\\
    |\mathcal D(h)|&\leq L^t\norm{h}_\infty
      &&\text{for every real function \(h\) on \(Y\)}.
      \label{eq:parity-functional-norm}
  \end{align}
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There is a measurable online selection rule, independent of the value
distributions, with the following property. Let $M=(E,\mathcal I)$ be any
finite known labeled matroid, and let $(S_e,V_e:e\in E)$ be mutually
independent nonnegative real random variables, with $S_e$ and $V_e$ having
the same arbitrary law $D_e$. Assume
$\Ex[\OPT_M(V)]<\infty$. The rule receives exactly the sample vector $S$
before arrivals and uses a seed $R$ independent of $S,V$.

For every measurable permutation rule $\pi$ depending on $M$, the laws
$(D_e)$, $S$, $V$, and $R$, the rule accepts an independent set $A$,
irrevocably deciding at each arrival using only the available history, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main}
 \Ex\left[\sum_{e\in A}V_e\right]
       \ge 2^{-310}\Ex[\OPT_M(V)].
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Disjoint-query certificates]\label{lem:transactions}
Let $V_0$ be finite, let its bits be independent Bernoulli random
variables, and let $\mathcal A\subseteq2^{V_0}$ be increasing with failure
probability $\delta>0$. An adaptive procedure queries each coordinate at
most once and divides its queries into transactions. The next query,
transaction boundaries, and stopping decisions depend only on the
transcript and, if desired, an independent auxiliary seed. Suppose the
number of transactions has a deterministic finite bound. A transaction
may be declared successful only if the positive bits queried within that
transaction alone form a certificate for $\mathcal A$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:certificate-budget}
 \Ex[\text{number of successful transactions}]
       \le\log(1/\delta).
\end{equation}
Here and below $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Order-oblivious selection with full-seed visibility]
\label{cor:secretary}
For each known finite labeled matroid $M=(E,\mathcal I)$, there is one
measurable randomized online rule $\mathcal S_M$ with the following
property. Fix any vector $w\in[0,\infty)^E$ of finite nonnegative weights
before all rule and arrival randomness. Without knowing $w$, the rule
draws its complete initial seed $Q$, independently of a uniformly random
permutation $\sigma$ of $E$, and fixes a possibly random prefix length
$K$ before any arrival. It observes the first $K$ label--weight pairs of
$\sigma$ in order and rejects those labels.

After this ordered prefix is observed and before any suffix arrival, an
adversary may know $M$, the entire fixed vector $w$, the ordered prefix,
and the complete seed $Q$, including $K$, the branch choice, and unused
coins. It may choose any
measurable permutation $\tau$ of the remaining labels as a function of
this information. The rule is not told the future suffix order and decides
irrevocably at each suffix arrival while maintaining an independent set.
Writing $A_{\mathcal S}$ for its accepted set, for every such adversary,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:secretary-guarantee}
 \Ex\left[\sum_{e\in A_{\mathcal S}}w_e\right]
 \ge 2^{-293}\OPT_M(w).
\end{equation}
The expectation is over the rule seed and random prefix, and over any
adversary randomization. The adversary cannot alter the random-prefix law
or choose the weights after observing the seed or prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Marked pivots]\label{lem:pivot-patterns}
Let $M$ be any finite matroid, and let $V$ be a set of $n$ nonloops.
Let $s\ge0$ be an integer.  Fix an ordered sequence of labeled
\emph{old occurrences}, each with a
mark in $\{0,1\}$, whose labels span $E$.  Also fix at most $s$ labeled
\emph{movable occurrences}.  Repetitions of labels are allowed in both
sequences.  Insert the movable occurrences into the old sequence in any
order and positions, and give each movable occurrence either mark.
For $f\in V$, its pivot is the first occurrence after whose insertion
$f$ is spanned; record that occurrence's mark.  The number of resulting
vectors of $n$ marks is at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pivot-pattern-bound}
 4^s\sum_{\ell=0}^{s}\binom n\ell,
\end{equation}
where $\binom n\ell=0$ for $\ell>n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A uniform family of residuals]\label{lem:pattern-family}
Fix $H$ and a true group $U_i$ of size $n=n_i\ge\kappa$.
Condition also on the parity and on the $D,C,T$ bits outside $U_i$,
but do not condition on their bits in $U_i$ or on whether $U_i$ is
listed.
There is a deterministic family $\mathfrak R_i\subseteq 2^{U_i}$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pattern-family-size}
 |\mathfrak R_i|\le
 \exp\left(\frac{1000\log\kappa}{\kappa}\,n\right)
\end{equation}
such that, whenever this group is listed and $z_h\le n/\kappa$, every
residual \eqref{eq:residual-set} obtained from witnesses
\eqref{eq:rank-witnesses} belongs to $\mathfrak R_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There is a uniform classical randomized algorithm which, given $G$ and
rational parameters $0<\eps<1$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, returns a nonnegative
rational number $\widehat Z$ such that
\[
 \Prb\bigl[(1-\eps)Z(G)\le \widehat Z\le(1+\eps)Z(G)\bigr]
 \ge 1-\delta.
\]
If $Z(G)=0$, the output is zero with certainty. The worst-case bit running
time is polynomial in the input encoding length, $\eps^{-1}$, and
$\log\delta^{-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:subdivision}
The real graph has $N$ vertices. Its perfect matchings are in
bijection with logical perfect matchings, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:real-partition}
 Z'=C_0 Z_\lambda,
 \qquad
 C_0=\prod_e\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le4p+1\\j\text{ even}}}t_j^e.
\end{equation}
On a noncentral real edge, its effective strength $B'$ equals its
activity. On the central edge of the path for $uv$, it equals
$B_{uv}$. Incident effective strengths differ by a factor of at most
two. For an internal vertex $x_j$, its maximum incident effective
strength is
\[
 T_j=
 \begin{cases}
 t_j,&1\le j\le2p,\\
 t_{j+1},&2p+1\le j\le4p.
 \end{cases}
\]
Its \emph{home terminal} is $u$ in the first case and $v$ in the
second. Every edge on its leg to its home has activity at least $T_j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Label-adapted quadrangulation]
\label{lem:quadrangulation}
The polygon of $\mathcal C$ has a quadrangulation such that every cell
side represents an admissible odd arc and the following hold in every
cell:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item some opposite pair of sides consists of good arcs;
 \item if both arcs in an opposite pair are long, both arcs in the
 other opposite pair are good.
\end{enumerate}
There are $(m-2)/2$ cells and $(m-4)/2$ interior diagonals.  One can
construct the quadrangulation in time polynomial in $m$ and the encoding
length of the label tree.

Each diagonal may be assigned any common label from the fixed sets at
its endpoints, used consistently in its two occurrences.  For a short
side, use the color of its actual cycle edge.  These choices need not
coincide with the auxiliary labels used in the construction.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparability within a cell]
\label{lem:cell-comparability}
Consider the four colored side chords of a cell, the first and last
cycle edges of each of its four arcs, and one leaf repair for each
good long arc.  The labels of any two edges in this collection have
tree distance at most $6$.  Consequently their activities lie within
a factor
\[
 A_0=1000D
\]
of one another.  The same conclusion holds after clamping every edge
activity to any common interval $[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Encodings with a bounded number of preimages]
\label{lem:encoding}
Every switch demand has an encoding $(A_P,B)$ by two perfect
matchings, and every error demand has encodings
$(A^{(j)},B^{(j)})$ for $j=0,1$, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item For each encoding $(A,B)$,
 $\rho(d)\le A_0^4\pi(A)\pi(B)$.
 \item For each encoding type and each fixed output pair, there are
 at most $\calT$ demand preimages.  This bound includes the choices
 of cycle, cell, opposite pair, and context.
 \item For an error demand, both guide matchings satisfy
 $C_X\subseteq B^{(j)}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:base-refresh}
The unit-activity partition function is computable by a dynamic program
on the label tree. With exact rational categorical choices, its tables
also produce an exact sample. The tables
can be computed with $O((b_{\rm tree}+1)(N+1)^3)$ arithmetic
operations on counts of $O(N\log(N+1))$ bits. Label and loop indices
use $O(\log(b_{\rm tree}+1)+\log(N+1))$ additional bits. Once the tables are
available, a sample uses polynomially many integer operations and at
most $4(b_{\rm tree}+N+1)$ rational categorical choices, each with at
most $N+1$ outcomes. A positive table also yields a matching by
entirely deterministic backtracking.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:bag-sampler}
Define $T,q,M$ by
\cref{eq:ladder-parameters,eq:ladder-update-count}, and put
\begin{align}
 \Lambda&=10Nq(T+1)
       \bigl(K+\lceil\log_2(ND+2)\rceil+1\bigr),
       \label{eq:ladder-lambda}\\
 s(\xi)&=\left\lceil20LM
       \bigl(\Lambda+\lceil\log_2(1/\xi)\rceil+1\bigr)\right\rceil
       \qquad(0<\xi<1).
       \label{eq:ladder-steps}
\end{align}
Initialize all slots to any one colored perfect matching and run the
exact chain for $s(\xi)$ steps. The resulting product law is at total
variation distance at most $\xi$ from $\nu$. In particular, any
top-tier slot has law within $\xi$ of the desired weighted matching
law.

All tables, state representations, and transition probabilities are
computable by rational arithmetic. Their sizes, arithmetic operation
counts, and rational bit lengths are polynomial in $N,D,K$,
$b_{\rm tree}$, $\log(1/\xi)$, and the bit lengths of the reference
activities. Exact rational choices here define an ideal process;
the bounded-bit implementation in \cref{sec:complexity} adds at most
$\xi$ to the total variation error.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:finite-random-choice}
Let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be nonnegative rational numbers summing to one.
Choose a uniform integer $J\in\{0,\ldots,2^k-1\}$ using exactly $k$
fair bits, and return the least index $i$ such that
$J/2^k<\sum_{j\le i}p_j$. The output law is at total variation
distance at most $2r\,2^{-k}$ from $(p_i)_{i=1}^r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:prescribed-degree}
For either family $\mathcal A=\mathcal F(G,f)$ or
$\mathcal A=\mathcal M_k(G)$, there are uniform classical randomized
algorithms with the following guarantees.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Given rational $0<\eps<1$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, the counting algorithm
returns a nonnegative rational $\widehat N$ such that
\[
 \Prb[(1-\eps)|\mathcal A|\le \widehat N\le(1+\eps)|\mathcal A|]
 \ge1-\delta.
\]
If $\mathcal A$ is empty, it returns zero with certainty. Its bit running
time on every execution is polynomial in the full input encoding length,
$\eps^{-1}$, and $\log\delta^{-1}$.
\item Given rational $0<\tau<1$, the sampling algorithm reports infeasibility
exactly when $\mathcal A$ is empty. Otherwise it returns a member $X$ of
$\mathcal A$ on every execution, and
\[
 \TV(\mathcal L(X),U_{\mathcal A})\le\tau,
\]
where $U_{\mathcal A}$ is the uniform law on $\mathcal A$ and
$\TV(\mu,\nu)=\frac12\sum_x|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|$. Its bit running time on every
execution is polynomial in the full input encoding length and $\tau^{-1}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:deletion-sampler}
Given a finite simple undirected unweighted graph $H_0$ whose vertices
and edges are explicitly listed, and a rational $0<\tau<1$, there is a
uniform classical randomized algorithm that reports infeasibility exactly
when $H_0$ has no perfect matching. Otherwise it returns a perfect
matching on every execution, and its output law is at total variation
distance at most $\tau$ from the uniform perfect-matching law. Its bit
running time on every execution is polynomial in the full input encoding
length and $\tau^{-1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
For every integer $r\ge4$, there is a constant $c_r>0$ such that every
finite simple $K_r$-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and average degree $d\ge2$
satisfies
\[
 \alpha(G)\ge c_r\frac{n\log d}{d}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Triangle mass from cross mass]
\label{thm:weighted-triangles}
For every $C\ge1$ there is a constant $C_{\triangle}(C)$ with the
following property.  If $G$ is a finite simple graph with positive
vertex weights $w$ satisfying \eqref{eq:cross-mass}, then
\[
 T_G(w)\le C_{\triangle}(C)M_G(w).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Triangle normalization and peeling]
\label{lem:triangle-peeling}
For a positive-weighted finite simple graph $G$, put
\[
 s_u=w(N_G(u)),\qquad
 c_{uv}=w(N_G(u)\cap N_G(v)),\qquad
 h_u=\sum_{v\in N_G(u)}w_vc_{uv}.
\]
Thus $h_u=2M_{G[N_G(u)]}(w)$ is twice the edge mass inside the
neighborhood of $u$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:triangle-normalizations}
 \sum_{\{u,v\}\in E(G)}w_uw_vc_{uv}=3T_G(w),
 \qquad
 \sum_{u\in V(G)}w_uh_u=6T_G(w).
\end{equation}
In particular, if every neighborhood has weight at most $L$, then
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:terminal-triangle-bound}
 T_G(w)\le \frac{L}{3}M_G(w).
\end{equation}

For every $\tau>0$, there is a spanning subgraph $G'$ obtained by
successive edge deletions such that every edge of $G'$ has common-neighbor
weight at least $\tau$ and
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:peeling-loss}
 T_{G'}(w)\ge T_G(w)-\tau M_G(w).
\end{equation}
For each nonisolated vertex of $G'$, its neighborhood and common-neighbor
weights, computed in $G'$, satisfy
\[
 s_u\ge\tau,\qquad h_u\ge\tau s_u.
\]
If $G$ satisfies \eqref{eq:cross-mass}, then so does $G'$,
with the same constant.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There are arbitrarily large integers \(m\) for which an \(m\)-vertex
finite simple graph \(G\) satisfies
\[
             \alpha(G)\le2
             \qquad\text{and}\qquad
             \cm(G)<\frac{m}{100}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:hadwiger}\label{cor:fractional-hadwiger}
There are finite nonempty simple graphs \(G\) of arbitrarily large
order \(m\) for which
\[
 h(G)<\frac{26m}{75}+\frac23
 <\frac m2\le\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G).
\]
Thus Hadwiger's conjecture and its fractional-coloring weakening
\(\chi_f(G)\le h(G)\) are false.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:entropy-support}
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty compact convex set of probability measures on a finite set, and let \(\rho\) minimize \(\mathsf D(\cdot\Vert q)\) on \(\mathcal P\).
Then \(\rho\) is positive on the union of the supports of measures in \(\mathcal P\).
For every \(\rho'\in\mathcal P\),
\[
 \mathsf D(\rho'\Vert q)-\mathsf D(\rho\Vert q)
 \ge \mathsf D(\rho'\Vert\rho).
\]
If \(\rho'\) is supported on a set \(S\), the right side is at least \(-\log\rho(S)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:terminal-cut}
Let \(R\subseteq\Omega_n^2\).
If no probability law supported on \(R\) satisfies \Cref{eq:raw-law-caps}, there are sets \(S\subseteq\Omega_n\) and \(E_0\subseteq\Omega_n^2\) such that
\[
 \mu(S)<1/M,\qquad \mu^2(E_0)<2^{-DN},
\]
and every pair in \(R\) either has an endpoint in \(S\) or belongs to \(E_0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:raw-to-graph}
Assume the conclusion of \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation} at a given sufficiently large \(n\).
For \(m=2^{C_0gN}\), the sampled graph defined in \Cref{sec:geometry} satisfies
\[
 \alpha(G)\le2,\qquad \cm(G)<m/100
\]
with probability \(1-\exp(-\Omega(m))\).
The implied positive constant is independent of \(n\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:matching-minor}
For every finite nonempty graph \(G\) of order \(m\),
\[
 \had(G)\le\frac{m+4\cm(G)+2}{3}.
\]
In particular, if \(\alpha(G)\le2\) and \(\cm(G)<m/100\), then
\[
 \had(G)<\frac{26m}{75}+\frac23<\frac m2\le\chi(G)
 \qquad(m\ge5).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:paired-frame-orbit}
Let \(A,A':U\to V\) and \(B,B':W\to V^*\) be injective maps between finite-dimensional spaces over \(\F\).
If
\[
 B\trans A=(B')\trans A',
\]
there is \(L\in\GL(V)\) with \(LA=A'\) and \(L^{-\mathsf T}B=B'\).
Thus based individually injective plus and minus frames with a prescribed Gram matrix form one orbit under the simultaneous primal and dual action.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:frame-images}
The following statements hold for all sufficiently large \(n\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item
The plus frame \([P,X]\) is uniform among injective maps.
Conditional on it, the minus columns are independent uniforms on the affine spaces prescribed in \Cref{eq:raw-frame-law}, followed only by the conditioning that \([Q,Y]\) is injective.
The failure probability of this last condition, before conditioning, is at most \(2^{2(d+h)-N}\) per component.

Given \(P,Q\), the channels \(X,Y\) are independent uniform-column draws on \(\ker Q\trans\) and \(\ker P\trans\), respectively, conditioned on \([P,X]\) and \([Q,Y]\) being injective.
The two rank-failure probabilities are exponentially small in \(N\).
Each channel frame alone is uniform among injective maps \(\F^h\to\F^N\).
For any fixed \(q\) independent vectors in its paired ambient space, the probability that transpose evaluation on their span is not injective is at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:channel-transpose-failure}
 2^{q-h+1}.
\end{equation}
The unconditional joint channel law is bounded above by a constant, depending on \(g,h\) but not on \(n\), times the completely independent uniform-column law.

\item
At independently sampled raw vertices and components, images of prescribed primal coefficient tuples that are independent separately at each vertex and sign are uniform subject to their individual injectivities and their prescribed same-vertex Gram matrices.
For tuples using channels as well, the same assertion holds conditionally on the full self-channel Gram matrices \(X_e\trans Y_e\); the relevant full Gram matrix is
\(\begin{psmallmatrix}E&0\\0&X_e\trans Y_e\end{psmallmatrix}\).

\item
Let a fixed tuple of nominal directions use arbitrary combinations of the two endpoints' primal and channel coefficients.
Compute its rank separately in each component and sign in the \emph{direct sum over both endpoints}, and let the total be \(t\).
For every preassigned \(\epsilon>0\), choosing \(M_0\) sufficiently large gives, under \(\mu^2\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:reference-image-cap}
 \PP\{\text{all those images equal prescribed vectors}\}
 \le 2^{-(1-\epsilon)tN}\qquad(t\ge1).
\end{equation}
This is valid for all possible ranks \(t\), including \(t=O(n)\), not only for bounded tuples.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:raw-intersections}
Let \(\sigma\) satisfy the joint cap in \Cref{eq:raw-law-caps}.
Outside a set of \(\sigma\)-probability \(2^{-\Omega(N)}\),
\[
 \sum_{e\in\cE}
  \dim\bigl(\im P_{1,e}\cap\im P_{2,e}\bigr)\le2D.
\]
For any unit outside that exceptional set and any
\(U_1\lambda_1=U_2\lambda_2\), both \(\lambda_i\) have total component rank at most \(2D\).
Each has a unique representation \((w_{i,l})_l\) vanishing at a strict majority of tags, and
\[
 |\{l:w_{i,l}\ne0\}|\le4D/g,\qquad
 \chi_*(w_1)=\chi_*(w_2).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Walsh estimates]\label{lem:walsh}
Let all weights below have absolute value at most one.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item
If \(x,y\) are independent uniform vectors and \(B(x,y)\) is a bilinear form of rank \(d\), then
\[
 \left|\E f(x)g(y)(-1)^{B(x,y)}\right|\le2^{-d/2}.
\]
Replacing either uniform law by a law of density at most \(C_i\) multiplies this bound by at most \(C_1C_2\).

\item
If \(\alpha,\beta\) are subprobability measures on \(\F^d\), with point masses at most \(p_1,p_2\), respectively, then
\[
 \left|\sum_{x,y}\alpha(x)\beta(y)f(x)g(y)(-1)^{x\cdot y}\right|
 \le2^{d/2}(p_1p_2)^{1/2}.
\]

\item
For independent uniform global \(N\)-bit vector slots in two groups, a cross-pairing character with coefficient matrix \(C\) has bit rank \(N\rank C\).
In particular, if its cross coefficient pattern is nonzero, its correlation against two bounded weights, one on each group, is at most \(2^{-N/2}\).
Arbitrary phases depending separately on the groups may be included in these weights.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:base-moments}
The span of $(1,z)(1,z)\trans$, $z\in\F^{d_{\mathrm b}}$, consists precisely of
symmetric $(1+d_{\mathrm b})$-by-$(1+d_{\mathrm b})$ matrices $Z$ satisfying
$Z_{ii}=Z_{0i}$ for every $i$.
For any $u$ distinct selectors, their evaluation vectors $p_s$ are
linearly independent if $j_*\ge u-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform mixing forms]\label{lem:generic-mixers}
For all sufficiently large $n$ one can choose the matrices
$L_j^{ef},R_j^{ef}$ and $M_a$ in \Cref{sec:geometry} so that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item\label{item:mixer-unary}
For every nonzero $x\in\cX$ of total component rank at most $K$,
every tag, label and flavor, and every fixing of the non-$Z$
base coordinates, the quadratic function
$T(x,\mathfrak a_l(s,z))$ of the $n$ remaining $Z$ bits has polar
rank at least $2(J-s_0)$.  It uses a space of linear forms on $Z$
of bounded dimension, independent of $n$.  This space can be
chosen before the non-$Z$ coordinates are fixed.
\item\label{item:mixer-binary}
For two distinct labels and any two flavors, every nonzero parity
of the indexed $L_j^{ef},R_j^{ef}$ evaluations between the two
point inputs, allowing each matrix in either order or both,
and optionally either or both orders of $E$, has bilinear-part
rank at least $n/5$.  Here a nonzero parity involving an $L$ or
$R$ evaluation means that at least one such indexed ordered
evaluation occurs.  The same rank bound holds for the three
parities consisting of $E$ alone, its reverse alone, or their sum.
\end{enumerate}
The choices are made before any unit law is selected.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Table flags and binary prescriptions]\label{lem:small-tables}
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For a fixed pair of leaves and a numerical small table,
admissibility is the intersection of two unary orientation
filters, one on each unit.  Its numerical coordinate data,
including injection and the bases of the effective spaces,
have bounded description length apart from the nominal
coefficient bases, which require $O(n)$ bits.
\item The key directions of the lists at either unit are jointly
independent modulo its table-coordinate spaces, component by
component and sign by sign.
\item Given \eqref{eq:recipe-scalars}, there is a prescription of
the binary $L,R$ evaluations between distinct atoms at each
endpoint, depending only on their tags, tester summaries and
$p$ bits, which makes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:recipe-gradients}
 r(v_{iz})(x)=
 \begin{cases}
  0,&x\text{ is an atom of the list toward }z,\\
  p_{z'}(\widetilde x),&x\text{ is an atom toward }z',
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
where $z'$ is the other endpoint of the opposite unit and
$\widetilde x$ is the matched atom there.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Gradient realization]\label{thm:gradient-realization}
Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying
\eqref{eq:recipe-scalars}, the binary prescriptions yielding
\eqref{eq:recipe-gradients}, equal matched keys, and an
admissible injecting small table.  Freeze their actual cross
Gram entries whenever either argument is a pin or a key
direction.  Then there are abstract cross bilinear forms on
the full nominal spaces, extending all these frozen entries,
whose primal-versus-channel entries satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:realized-gradients}
 u_zU_i=r(v_{iz})\quad\text{on }\cX
 \qquad(i\text{ and }z\text{ in opposite units}).
\end{equation}
Only the primal-versus-channel entries need be prescribed in
the final test.  Their number is at most
$16|\cE|h\dim\cB=O(n)$, with its coefficient fixed before
$M_0$.  Agreement of the actual cross Grams with these entries
produces all four cross holes, with witnesses $(v_{iz},v_{zi})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Collision criterion]\label{prop:collision}
Let $\sigma$ be a unit law in \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation},
and let $\widetilde\sigma$ be a restriction of it of relative
mass at least $2^{-o(N)}$, decomposed into leaves satisfying
\eqref{eq:final-leaf-minentropy}.  Mix the leaves with their
actual masses in $\widetilde\sigma$.
Suppose accepted numerical queries as above, with their
leaf-pair choices of table and separate filters, satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:overlap-criterion}
 \E_{\text{independent leaf pair}}
       \int d_A d_B\,d\nu_n\ge 2^{-o(N)}.
\end{equation}
Then two independent units from the original $\sigma$ have
all four cross holes with probability at least
\begin{equation}\label{eq:collision-conclusion}
 2^{-(k_{\max}+.03)N-o(N)}.
\end{equation}
It suffices to obtain \eqref{eq:overlap-criterion} after skipping
some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of
numerical options.  Positive subsequential constants and
inverse-polynomial overlap bounds both suffice.  In particular,
this conclusion contradicts a sequence violating
\Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Phase alternative]
\label{thm:phase-alternative}
Suppose a marked-unit law is obtained by restricting an admissible
law in \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation} to mass at least \(10^{-12}\),
and \(\Delta_O\ne0\) throughout. For all sufficiently large \(n\),
one can retain a sublaw of fixed positive relative mass, bounded below
using only the early parameters, such that one of the following holds
for independent draws \(A,B\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item every nontrivial phase mean
\[
 \E(-1)^{u_{B,S}(\Delta_A)+u_{A,R}(\Delta_B)},
 \qquad(S,R)\ne(\varnothing,\varnothing),
\]
has absolute value less than \(.005\);
\item a componentwise cover of total dimension at most \(d_0\)
covers every \(\Delta_O\), and every displayed mean for which
\(|S|=1\) or \(|R|=1\) is \(2^{-\Omega(N)}\).
\end{enumerate}
The cover may depend on the law and on \(n\). The constants in its
dimension bound and in the relative mass bound do not depend on the
later selector or channel sizes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Injection on accepting pairs]
\label{lem:injection}
Let a prepared marked-unit law have final pins of total dimension
at most \(K\), and mixed marginals at most \(M2^{o(N)}\mu\).
Let \({\cal A}\) be a pair event for independent draws, of probability
at least \(N^{-c_0}\) for some fixed \(c_0\).
For each fixed draw suppose its accepting opposite units form a
member of a fixed family of cardinality at most \(2^{C_sN}\).
Assume \(C_s\) is fixed before \(h\).
For every fixed \(\eps>0\), by choosing \(h\) sufficiently large
in terms of \(K,C_s,\eps,g\), the proportion of pairs in
\({\cal A}\) failing the small-table injection conditions is at
most \(\eps\), for all sufficiently large \(n\).
For the unconditional pair event the accepting family has one
member.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Consequences of a tiny cover]
\label{lem:tiny-cover}
Suppose the second alternative of \Cref{thm:phase-alternative}
holds, and write
\[
 F(A,B)=u_{B,\{1,2\}}(\Delta_A).
\]
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The matrix \(F\) on the finite support has rank at most
\(d_0N\).  Its alternating part \(F+F\trans\) has rank at most
\(2d_0N\).  If
\(\PP\{F(A,B)+F(B,A)=0\}\to0\), there is a restriction of
mass \(2^{-o(N)}\) on which that alternating part is
identically zero.
\item If \(F(A,A)=0\) throughout, then for either fixed
\(c\in\F\),
\begin{equation}
 \PP\{u_{B,1}(\Delta_A)=u_{B,2}(\Delta_A)
       =u_{A,1}(\Delta_B)=u_{A,2}(\Delta_B)=c\}
       \ge c_1N^{-4}
 \label{eq:tiny-four-phases}
\end{equation}
for a positive fixed \(c_1\) and all large \(n\).
\item In part \textup{(b)}, one can apply the second peeling
so that the event in \Cref{eq:tiny-four-phases} is determined
by the two leaves.  At most \(4K_1+2d_0<u_0\) additional
image directions are needed.  The same \(\Omega(N^{-4})\)
leaf-pair mass survives the exponentially small discards.
On admissible small tables, the contractions on the old
\(\lambda_i\)'s then equal the actual contractions.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Status preparation]
\label{prop:status-preparation}
Along a subsequence, the unit law can be prepared with final
pin dimension at most \(K\) and the final per-leaf bounds of
\Cref{lem:peeling}, at relative mass cost \(2^{-o(N)}\), so
that one of the following descriptions applies.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There is no prediction as in \Cref{def:prediction}
on the first-peeled law. The effective spaces are still the
first ones. For independent units, the mass admitting an
admissible injecting small table is greater than \(.99\).
\item A prediction with fixed \(\alpha_i,c\) and common
classes \(e_i\) is retained. The old marks and exceptions
are preserved, and \Cref{eq:prediction} has uniform \(o(1)\)
error on every retained unit. The mass admitting an
admissible injecting table satisfying
\Cref{eq:phase-compatibility} is bounded below by a positive
constant.
\item Both prediction classes are zero, and every retained
unit satisfies the exact identities
\[
 p_i=T(\lambda_i,\cdot)+a
 \quad\text{on all of }\cX,\qquad i=1,2.
\]
There is a set of leaf pairs of mass at least
\(c_2N^{-4}\) under the final leaf mixture, for a fixed
\(c_2>0\), with phase compatibility determined by the
two leaves. For each such pair one can choose a specific
injecting compatible table whose two separate orientation
admissibility filters have masses at least \(a_0>0\).
The constants \(c_2,a_0\) are independent of \(n\).
\end{enumerate}
In every case the mixed joint density is at most
\(2^{(D+o(1))N}\mu^2\), and its individual marginals are at
most \(M2^{o(N)}\mu\).
Relative to the stored leaf bases and pin images, all numerical
table formats, unary statuses, old-mark coordinates and exception-set
descriptions have bounded length in \(n\). The extra exact pins
are used only in case \textup{(iii)}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Affine-slice comparison]
\label{lem:synthetic-slice}
Fix a selector, a flavor, and a fixed number \(d\) of affine
parameter variables.  Write a random affine coefficient map as
\[
 C(t,u)=p_s\otimes(t,z_0t+Lu),
 \qquad (t,u)\in\F\oplus\F^d.
 \]
Assume the flavor retains an \(n\)-bit \(Z\)-block absent from
\(E\).  Suppose we condition the affine coefficients on
\(C\trans EC=G\), where \(G\) is fixed, this event has probability
at least a fixed \(\beta>0\), and it depends on no \(Z\)
coefficient.
Let \({\cal T}_n\) be any common test of absolute value at most
one on the image column arrays \((P_eC,Q_eC)_e\), using a fixed
set of components.  Its empirical average over the conditioned
affine coefficients, at a raw orientation, has variance
\[
 O(2^{-N/2}+2^{2d+1-n})
 \]
around its mean under uniform injective image column arrays
with internal Gram \(G\).
The constants may depend on the fixed column counts and
\(\beta\), but the estimate is uniform over the tests
\({\cal T}_n\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform histogram control]\label{lem:histogram-control}
Fix a query shape, a constant $C_L$, and an integer $F$. Consider any
collection of normalized leaf laws $\pi$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:histogram-leaf-cap}
 \pi\le 2^{C_LN}\mu^2.
\end{equation}
The following assertions are uniform over those leaves and over the
bounded numerical choices of a query.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $A_n$ is a sequence of slot sets with
$\omega_n(A_n)\to0$, then the probability that the unfiltered query
key belongs to $A_n$, averaged on any choice of leaves, tends to zero.
Equivalently, the averaged key laws are uniformly absolutely continuous
in this asymptotic small-set sense.
\item On each leaf, choose any $F$ binary flags of the orientation and
query parameters. Let $\mathcal H_{\pi,n}$ be the family of
unnormalized key densities obtained by filtering by any event of the
orientation and the flag values. For every $\eps>0$, this family has an
$L^1(\omega_n)$ $\eps$-net of cardinality bounded independently of $n$
and of the leaf, for all sufficiently large $n$. The net itself may
depend on the leaf.
\item Both conclusions persist after restricting the query to $\cK_n$
and expressing the subdensities relative to $\nu_n$. In particular these
subdensities are uniformly integrable: for every $\eta>0$ there is
$R<\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, all their tails
above $R$ have integral at most $\eta$.
\end{enumerate}
The flag functions may vary with the leaf and with $n$. The number of
flags is fixed. No bound on the normalized marginal of an individual
leaf is assumed here.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gram normalization]\label{lem:histogram-gram-normalization}
Let $a$ plus slots and $b$ minus slots in one ambient component be
independent uniform vectors, and prescribe their entire $a$ by $b$ Gram
matrix. If $a+b\le N/2$, the probability of that prescription together
with injectivity in each mode is
\[
 2^{-ab}\bigl(1+O(2^{-N+a+b})\bigr),
\]
uniformly in the prescribed matrix. The same statement holds for a
fixed collection of independent endpoint/component groups, with the
sum of their Gram-bit counts in place of $ab$ and a fixed factor in the
error bound. In particular, for a bounded number of slots all relevant
Gram normalizations and their ratios are bounded above and below by
positive constants, uniformly in the nominal inputs.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison of two bounded batches]
\label{lem:histogram-batch-comparison}
Consider two bounded batches of prescribed nominal columns in one raw
endpoint, or in two independent raw endpoints. Suppose their union is
nominally independent in every endpoint, component, and mode. Let $F$
and $G$ be bounded functions of the separate image batches, respectively.
The difference between their joint raw expectation and the product of
their separate raw expectations is
\[
 O\bigl(\norm{F}_\infty\norm{G}_\infty 2^{-N/2}\bigr).
\]
The bound is uniform in the independent nominal columns and all their
prescribed same-endpoint Gram entries. The functions may also depend
on the fixed nominal inputs determining their own batch.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Product tests under the key reference]
\label{lem:reference-product}
For a fixed query shape and arbitrary global single-key functions
$f_{j,n}$ with $\abs{f_{j,n}}\le1$,
\[
 \int\prod_jf_{j,n}(k_j)\,d\nu_n
 =\prod_j\int f_{j,n}\,d\Omega_{l_j,q_j,n}
   +O(2^{-N/2}).
\]
The bound is uniform over the functions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Many queries and prescribed cells]
\label{lem:histogram-many-queries}
Fix a bounded query shape. There are constants $c_1,c_2>0$, independent
of any key-space partition, with the following property. Put
$\ell=\lfloor c_1n\rfloor$ and repeat the query independently $\ell$
times at a common orientation. Let $A_1,\ldots,A_\ell$ be cells of a
partition of the full slot space, with weights
$w_j=\omega_n(A_j)$. Suppose the partition has bounded size and its
nonempty weights have a positive lower bound along the sequence under
consideration. Conditional on any nominal inputs whose queried columns
are jointly independent in every endpoint, component, and mode, the
raw image probability that query $j$ lies in $A_j$ is at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:histogram-many-query-bound}
 2^{c_2\ell}\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}w_j
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $n$. How large $n$ must be may depend on the
partition and its weight bound. The constants $c_1,c_2$ do not.

The probability, over the repeated fresh parameters, that the required
nominal independence fails tends to zero exponentially in $n$, uniformly
over the common orientation.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Typicality of common input-and-key tests]
\label{lem:typicality}
Let $F_n$ be a uniformly bounded common function of the inputs and
keys of a fixed bounded query, with no other orientation dependence.
Put
\[
 A_n(O)=\E_z F_n(z,K(O,z)),\qquad
 m_n=\E_{O\sim\mu^2,z}F_n(z,K(O,z)).
\]
For every fixed $\eps>0$, under \eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps},
\[
 \rho_n\{\abs{A_n-m_n}>\eps\}=2^{-\Omega(n)}.
\]
Repeated labels in the query are allowed. The constants may depend on
the query and $\eps$, but the estimate is uniform over tests with the
given sup bound. The exceptional set may depend on the test.

For a query at just one endpoint, its raw variance about its raw mean
is $2^{-\Omega(n)}$. This variance bound is also uniform when an
arbitrary external input-and-image datum is fixed as an argument of
the test.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Binary mixing]\label{lem:binary-mixing}
Fix a query template whose labels are distinct at each used endpoint.
Impose the off-position Gram zeros of $\cK_n$ and a consistent fixed
specification of the within-endpoint ordered $L,R$ evaluations used
in \Cref{sec:realization}. Let $\mathcal A_n(O,z)$ be their joint
indicator. There is a template constant $\kappa>0$ such that, outside
an exponentially small set of orientations under
\eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:binary-mixing}
 \E_z\mathcal A_n(O,z)\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)
 =\kappa\prod_j\E_{z_j}w_j(O,z_j)+O(2^{-c n})
\end{equation}
uniformly over all unary weights with $\abs{w_j}\le1$. These weights
may depend on the entire fixed orientation. The input laws may be
conditioned separately on feasible diagonal values or tester summaries.
The exceptional set is independent of the unary weights.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic signs on affine subspaces]
\label{lem:histogram-quadratic-bias}
Let $Q$ be a quadratic function on a binary vector space and let its
polar form have rank $2r$. Its uniform sign bias has magnitude at
most $2^{-r}$. On an affine subspace of codimension $c$, the restricted
polar rank is at least $2r-2c$, and its sign bias is at most
$2^{-r+c}$ whenever this bound is less than one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unary reference law and base-status positivity]
\label{lem:unary-positivity}
Fix an endpoint, tag, label, flavor, and feasible tester summary with
diagonal $q$. For a bounded number of common global key tests, its
empirical conditional key frequencies differ from
$\Omega_{l,q,n}$ by any prescribed fixed tolerance except on
exponentially small mixed mass under
\eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps}.

At each unit, let $C_i\subset\cX$ be any orientation-dependent space
of dimension at most $K^2$ all of whose elements have total component
rank at most $K$, and choose any basis. Fix a sequence of global
single-key sets $A_n$ with
$\Omega_{l,q,n}(A_n)\ge\delta>0$. Except on exponentially small mixed
mass, every basis assignment has, conditional on the tester summary
and on $K_i\in A_n$, fraction at least
$(7/8)2^{-\dim C_i}$.

For the full generic flavor and inputs conditional just on $q$, the
following conservative constant is valid:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-base-fraction}
 \beta=2^{-K^2-1}4^{-(g^2+1)}>0.
\end{equation}
For every feasible specified tester summary and basis assignment,
outside an exponentially small exceptional set,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:histogram-base-cell-lower}
 \PP_z\{K_i\in A_n,\ \text{the specified summary and basis bits}\mid q\}
 \ge\beta\,\Omega_{l,q,n}(A_n).
\end{equation}
In particular each joint choice of the role $a(\operatorname{atom})$
and the basis bits has this lower bound, after choosing a compatible
summary. Both roles are available for either possible generic $q$.

The lower constants do not depend on $\delta$, on the key tests, or on
the orientation-dependent choice of $C_i$. The onset of the
asymptotics and the exceptional-set constants may depend on a fixed
positive lower bound $\delta$. The exceptional set is allowed to
depend on the prescribed tests: there is no simultaneous assertion
over all measurable key sets at one orientation.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Weak product comparison]\label{thm:weak-product}
Let $W_n$ be any sequence of real functions on $\cK_n$ with
$\norm{W_n}_\infty\le B$, where $B$ is fixed. Extend it to the product
of the single-key spaces with the same bound. For every $\eps>0$
there are constants $L,C<\infty$, independent of $n$, and functions
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weak-product-approximant}
 S_n(k_1,\ldots,k_r)
   =\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}\prod_{j=1}^{r}f_{a,j,n}(k_j),
 \qquad
 \abs{c_{a,n}}\le C,\quad \abs{f_{a,j,n}}\le1,
\end{equation}
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For arbitrary global unary functions $g_{j,n}$ of bound one,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weak-product-reference}
 \abs{\int(W_n-S_n)\prod_jg_{j,n}(k_j)\,d\nu_n}\le\eps
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $n$.
\item Under any mixed unit law satisfying
\eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps}, outside an exponentially small
exceptional set of orientations,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weak-product-actual}
 \sup_{\abs{w_j}\le1}
 \abs{\E_z\mathcal A_n(O,z)
       (W_n-S_n)(K(O,z))\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)}\le\eps.
\end{equation}
The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation
and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is
independent of these weights.
\end{enumerate}
The functions $f_{a,j,n}$ are global key functions; they can be chosen
to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such
indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on
the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on $B,\eps$ and
the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on $n$.

An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply
\eqref{eq:weak-product-actual} without changing it. In particular,
after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to
unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the
filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for
an arbitrary additional joint input filter.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Global projections with adaptive filter choices]
\label{lem:limit-global-projection}
Let $(K_n,\nu_n)$ be finite probability spaces. On each first-side leaf
$L$ and each second-side leaf $L'$ let there be a family of subdensities.
Assume that, for each fixed $R<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$, their
truncations at height $R$ have $L^1(\nu_n)$ nets of uniformly bounded
size, with the nets chosen using their own leaf only. The bounds may
depend on $R,\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or the leaf.

For every $R<\infty$ and $\eta>0$, there are deterministic partitions
$\mathcal P_n$ of uniformly bounded size such that the following holds.
These partitions may depend on the leaf laws, but are chosen before
the leaves are sampled.
For independent leaves, choose a member $f$ and a member $g$ of the two
truncated families, allowing either choice to depend on both leaves.
If $P_n$ is conditional expectation onto $\mathcal P_n$, then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:limit-projection-error}
\E\bigl|\pair{f}{g}-\pair{P_nf}{P_ng}\bigr|\le\eta.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for every deterministic refinement of
$\mathcal P_n$ chosen independently of the sampled leaves.
Multiplication of the discrepancy by any indicator determined by the
leaf pair does not increase the bound.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Common signature model]
\label{lem:limit-model}
There is a subsequence and a common limiting experiment with the
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For each tag and diagonal bit $(l,q)$ there is a compact
bit-sequence space $\Xi_{l,q}$ with reference law $m_{l,q}$.
For each key shape there is a compact tuple-test space $\Upsilon$
with reference law $\rho$. Its single-position projections
$\xi_\ell$ have the independent laws $m_{l_\ell,q_\ell}$.
\item A base orientation array $\theta$ contains its bounded discrete
metadata and its single-atom status measures. For a unary type
$t=(i,l,s,\varphi,q)$ and a full numerical status $\upsilon$, these measures
have jointly measurable densities
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:limit-unary-densities}
h^\theta_{t,\upsilon}:\Xi_{l,q}\longrightarrow[0,1],\qquad
\sum_\upsilon h^\theta_{t,\upsilon}=1\quad m_{l,q}\text{-almost everywhere}.
\end{equation}
For the full generic flavor, the sum of these densities over statuses
with any specified role and basis vector in the recorded actual dimension
is bounded below by a positive construction constant, almost everywhere.
Compatible finer tester
requirements have the lower fractions supplied by
\Cref{lem:unary-positivity}.
\item There is first a random limiting leaf-pair record $Z$, which
includes two conditional laws $\Lambda_A,\Lambda_B$ of the arrays and
their finite flag vectors. Conditional on $Z$, the two orientation
records are drawn independently from these laws. After flags are
dropped and $Z$ is averaged out, $\theta_A,\theta_B$ are iid.
\item Every discrete assertion of table usability, injection, and
prepared phase compatibility is retained in this experiment. In
particular, the positive mass of a passed compatible injecting table
from \Cref{prop:status-preparation} is retained. On the no-prediction
branch the mass of a passed injecting table is at least $.99$.
On a predicted branch the prediction relation is exact in the limiting
status measures outside its stored exceptions.
\end{enumerate}
All single-key tests used to define $\Xi_{l,q}$ are functions of global
keys only.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Passage of vanishing overlaps]
\label{lem:limit-zero-product}
Assume \eqref{eq:limit-vanishing-overlap}. For almost every $Z$, the
measures $\eta_A(Z),\eta_B(Z)$ of every usable option are absolutely
continuous with respect to $\rho$, and their densities have product zero
$\rho$-almost everywhere.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar solvability on positive mass]
\label{lem:status-span}
In each positive-mass alternative of
\Cref{prop:status-preparation}, the common experiment has positive mass
of passed injecting tables for which the scalar system is soluble,
robustly under the exclusions needed below. On the no-prediction branch
this holds whenever the total exclusions stay within $B_*$ per endpoint.
On a predicted branch it holds after the stored exceptions and any
further bounded exclusions leaving generic labels.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fresh lists of at most seven generators]
\label{lem:fresh-lists}
On each scalar-soluble pair from \Cref{lem:status-span}, further bounded
exclusions can be made so that every scalar solution on the resulting
four edge spans can be realized by between one and seven available
generators per edge. The two endpoint labels of each generator are
retained with its certificate, and all labels used at an endpoint are
distinct across its two incident lists. Every realized matched
position has positive status overlap.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Positive-mass overlap]
\label{prop:positive-overlap}
For every positive-mass alternative of
\Cref{prop:status-preparation}, some fixed numerical option has expected
unnormalized successful-query overlap bounded below by a positive
constant along a subsequence. Consequently it satisfies
\eqref{eq:overlap-criterion}. This conclusion includes the prepared
restrictions of reciprocal mass $2^{o(N)}$ permitted there.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Superlevel sets from all-filter nets]
\label{lem:rare-superlevel-nets}
Consider the family of unnormalized successful base-query densities
on a prepared leaf, allowing every orientation-only filter.
Suppose a member \(d\) has total mass at least \(b_0>0\).
Uniformly over the prepared leaves and the finite formats,
there are constants \(t,\delta_0>0\) such that, for every sufficiently
small fixed \(\epsilon>0\), a bounded family of reference sets contains
a set \(W\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \nu(W)\ge\delta_0/2,\qquad
 \nu\{k\in W:d(k)<t/4\}\le4\epsilon/t.
 \label{eq:rare-net-superlevel}
\end{equation}
The family depends on the leaf, format, and \(\epsilon\), but not on
the orientation-only filter subsequently selected.
The constants \(t,\delta_0\) can be fixed before \(\epsilon\).
\end{lemma}
